title: SEMI Sees Americas Fab Tool Spending Double to US$40.6B by 2029 as TSMC, Intel, Micron, Samsung Expand
key_facts: SEMI's latest report (via TechNews) projects global 300mm fab equipment spending of about USD 149 billion in 2026, up 31% from USD 113 billion in 2025, reaching USD 227 billion in 2029.
Equipment spending in the Americas, largely US-driven, is projected to more than double from USD 18.1 billion in 2026 to USD 40.6 billion in 2029.
SEMI expects construction to start on 20 new 300mm fabs or lines worldwide in 2026 and 18 in 2027, of which three and four are in the US.
Fab construction spending is forecast at nearly USD 48 billion in 2026, USD 63 billion in 2027 and USD 68 billion in 2028.
Joe Stockunas, SEMI Americas president, said US semiconductor-related investments exceed USD 800 billion, with more than USD 200 billion in Phoenix.
Key US projects named: Intel, TSMC and Samsung logic and foundry expansions, Micron DRAM, Texas Instruments analog; Intel and Micron urged Taiwanese suppliers to set up in the US (The Elec).
quote_evidence: According to TechNews, SEMI’s latest report projects global 300mm fab equipment spending to rise from US$113 billion in 2025 to approximately US$149 billion in 2026, up 31% YoY, before reaching US$227 billion in 2029.
As TechNews highlights, SEMI expects 300mm fab equipment spending in the Americas, largely driven by U.S. investment, to more than double from US$18.1 billion in 2026 to US$40.6 billion in 2029.
SEMI expects construction to begin on 20 new 300mm fabs or production lines worldwide in 2026 and another 18 in 2027, excluding R&D-only facilities.
why_it_matters_hint: Rising US chip-factory equipment spending points to more chip production outside Asia.
event_date: Reported 14 Oct 2026 from SEMICON West 2026 (day of the SEMI remarks not stated)
notes: TrendForce credits TechNews for the SEMI figures, so TechNews is the credited source; the TechNews original was not opened and the link is the TrendForce page.
